steps: No/minor bleeding with platelets >20–30: often observe.
Treat if bleeding or very low count: corticosteroids (prednisolone or dexamethasone) ± IVIG for rapid rise.
Life-threatening bleeding: IVIG + IV methylprednisolone + platelet transfusion (and consider TXA).
Second-line: TPO-receptor agonists, rituximab, or splenectomy.
Avoid antiplatelets/anticoagulants; confirm diagnosis (exclude secondary causes).

drugRefs.why: Standard first-line therapy to reduce immune platelet destruction.

drugRefs.freq: once daily for 4 days (may repeat cycles)
drugRefs.why: Alternative first-line regimen giving faster responses than prolonged prednisolone tapers.

drugRefs.dose: 1 g/kg/day for 1–2 days (or 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days)
drugRefs.why: Produces a rapid rise in platelets when urgent (active bleeding, pre-procedure) — added to steroids.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Disorders of Platelets and Vessel Wall (Ch. 120)
International Consensus Report on the Investigation and Management of Primary ITP

drugRefs.why: High-dose IV steroid combined with IVIG and platelet transfusion for critical bleeding.
Reserved for life-threatening haemorrhage; consumed rapidly, so given with IVIG and steroids.
Adjunct to reduce mucosal/menstrual bleeding; not a substitute for raising the platelet count.

drugRefs.dose: 50 mg once daily (adjust to platelet response; 25 mg in East Asian patients/hepatic impairment)
drugRefs.why: Stimulates platelet production; second-line for persistent/chronic ITP.

refs: International Consensus Report on the Investigation and Management of Primary ITP

confirm: Isolated thrombocytopenia with otherwise normal counts/film and no alternative cause; bleeding risk relates to platelet count.

investigations.test: Exclude secondary causes (HIV, HCV, drugs, SLE)

disposition: Outpatient if stable; admit if bleeding/very low.
